To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MCs can be activated by fungal pathogens and their components and that they can contribute significantly to the defense against fungal infections.

MCs are activated during infection with fungi, that MCs can detect fungi, that MC effector mechanisms contribute to the defense against fungi, and that the MCs are a potential target in the treatment of fungal infections.

(1) MCs can recognize fungal pathogens by several mechanisms; (2) MCs are able to produce a broad spectrum of antifungal effector molecules, including reactive oxygen species (ROS), reactive nitrogen species, and proteases; (3) MCs are involved in the regulation of the innate immune response to fungal pathogens; (4) the MC response can be beneficial for the host, but also detrimental; and (5) MCs can contribute to the development of fungal diseases.
